title: London System
author: LlamaChess Repertoire
description: The London System (1.d4 d5 2.Bf4) — 28 interactive lines with casual move-by-move notes.

steps.title: G7 Heist — Punishing ...Bd6
steps.theory: Let's learn the London system! Before we get started, I have to warn you: this opening is basically the same five boring moves over and over and nobody will be your friend. If you're ok with that, then let's get started with pawn to d4.

steps.title: 1.d4
steps.theory: Let's get started with pawn to d4.

steps.title: d5
steps.theory: Black plays d5 — the most common response. Let's continue with the London!

steps.title: 2.Bf4
steps.theory: Second move of the London is bishop to f4.

steps.title: e6
steps.theory: Solid ...e6 from Black. We'll continue with our regular London setup: pawn to e3.

steps.title: 3.e3
steps.theory: The classic London pyramid begins. Black tries ...Bd6 to trade dark-squared bishops.

steps.title: Bd6
steps.theory: Black has abandoned the guard of the g7 pawn — let's play queen to g4 to attack it.

steps.title: 4.Qg4
steps.theory: Black has BLUNDERED! And this was their most common move too!! Before we recapture the bishop, we can take a free pawn with queen to g7.

steps.title: 5.Qxg7
steps.theory: Black tries ...Qf6. Before we take back the bishop, let's trade queens — queen takes queen on f6.

steps.title: Nxf6
steps.theory: NOW we can finally take back the bishop — pawn to f4. A free pawn is a free pawn!

steps.title: F-Pawn Folly — Crushing ...e5
steps.theory: Some opponents try ...f6 to blunt your bishop on f4. Don't panic — they often follow up with ...e5 and walk into a miniature attack.

steps.title: 2.Bf4
steps.theory: Bishop out to f4 — the London way.

steps.title: f6
steps.theory: ...f6 is passive but common at club level.

steps.title: 3.e3
steps.theory: Regular London stuff: pawn to e3.

steps.title: e5
steps.theory: Black just gave us a free pawn! This has happened in over a million games. Take on e5.

steps.title: fxe5
steps.theory: Instead of bishop taking back — we have an even better move! Queen to h5 check.

steps.title: g6
steps.theory: Now queen takes pawn on e5 with check. Black just lost the game in like five moves.

steps.title: Rook Lure — vs Symmetrical ...Bf5
steps.theory: When Black mirrors your bishop to f5, break out of autopilot London — strike in the center with c4.

steps.title: Bf5
steps.theory: Black goes for the symmetrical ...Bf5. Time to break the mirror — pawn to c4.

steps.title: dxc4
steps.theory: It looks like we gave away a pawn, but e3 opens the diagonal for our light-squared bishop.

steps.title: 4.e3
steps.theory: Black tries ...b5 to hold the extra pawn.

steps.title: b5
steps.theory: Huge blunder! Queen to f3 hits the rook on a8.

steps.title: c6
steps.theory: Even better: bishop takes knight on b8, discovering an attack on the f5 bishop.

steps.title: Rxb8
steps.theory: Free bishop! Queen takes on f5. A pawn for a bishop — that's a good trade.

steps.title: C7 Sting — Nc3 vs ...c5
steps.theory: When Black plays ...c5 early, knight to c3 sets up a nasty Nb5 fork trap that catches half your opponents.

steps.title: 3.e3
steps.theory: The next normal London move is pawn to e3.

steps.title: c5
steps.theory: Black goes for the ...c5 break. Break away from the usual setup — knight to c3.

steps.title: 4.Nc3
steps.theory: Black's most common move is actually a BLUNDER. We hop the knight to b5, threatening a fork on c7.

steps.title: Nc6
steps.theory: Black pushes ...e5 to challenge the center.

steps.title: 5.Nb5
steps.theory: Take with the bishop on e5.

steps.title: 6.Bxe5
steps.theory: Pawn takes knight — our e5 pawn is powerful.

steps.title: 7.dxe5
steps.theory: Incredible sequence: queen SACRIFICE on d5!

steps.title: Ne4
steps.theory: Black has to take the queen.

steps.title: 8.Qxd5
steps.theory: Knight to c7+, forking king and queen!

steps.title: 9.Nc7+
steps.theory: Win the queen back — knight takes on d5.

steps.title: 10.Nxd5
steps.theory: Lock Black in with c4. We are crushing — just don't castle queenside because ...Ne4 eyes f2.

steps.title: Queen Ransom — vs ...c5 ...Nc6
steps.theory: Black plays ...c5 before ...Nf6? This line transposes into Jobava London territory — a personal favorite.

steps.title: 3.e3
steps.theory: Don't grab the pawn — keep the center with e3.

steps.title: Nc6
steps.theory: Black develops the knight to c6.

steps.title: 4.Nc3
steps.theory: Trap time: knight to c3, aiming for b5 and the c7 fork.

steps.title: 5.Nb5
steps.theory: OUR OPPONENT FELL FOR THE TRAP! Knight to b5 immediately.

steps.title: 6.c3
steps.theory: Block with c3 — the c7 fork threat lives.

steps.title: 7.Bxe5
steps.theory: Win a pawn: bishop takes on e5.

steps.title: 9.Qxd5
steps.theory: Queen to d5 wins another pawn with a huge lead in development.

steps.title: Main Line Pyramid
steps.theory: The canonical London: build the c3-d4-e3 pyramid, develop knights to f3 and d2, and enjoy a rock-solid game.

steps.title: 2.Bf4
steps.theory: Bf4 before e3 — the accelerated London.

steps.title: 3.e3
steps.theory: Lock the bishop outside the pawn chain with e3.

steps.title: 5.Nbd2
steps.theory: Knight to d2 supports the center without blocking the c-pawn.

steps.title: 6.c3
steps.theory: Complete the famous pyramid with c3. The center is locked and your setup is complete.

steps.title: King's Indian Setup — vs ...g6
steps.theory: When Black fianchettos, the London still works — same structure, just watch the ...c5 and ...Qb6 breaks.

steps.title: Nf6
steps.theory: Black prepares a King's Indian with ...g6.

steps.title: 2.Bf4
steps.theory: Bf4 anyway — the London doesn't care.

steps.title: g6
steps.theory: The g7 bishop will stare at your center.

steps.title: 3.e3
steps.theory: e3 keeps our bishop safe from ...Ng4 tricks.

steps.title: 5.h3
steps.theory: A small prophylaxis move — h3 stops ...Ng4.

steps.title: 6.Nbd2
steps.theory: Nbd2 finishes development. Same London plans apply.

steps.title: Early ...c5 vs 1...Nf6
steps.theory: Black tries ...c5 before settling on d5. Meet it calmly — e3 and c3 keep your structure intact.

steps.title: 3.e3
steps.theory: Don't panic — e3 solidifies the center.

steps.title: 4.c3
steps.theory: c3 keeps the d4 pawn safe and completes the pyramid.

steps.title: Dutch Defense — vs 1...f5
steps.theory: Someone plays the Dutch? Fine — develop normally and let them weaken their own kingside.

steps.title: 2.Bf4
steps.theory: Bf4 targets c7 and keeps development smooth.

steps.title: 4.Nf3
steps.theory: Nf3 develops with tempo on the center.

steps.title: 5.Nbd2
steps.theory: Nbd2 — same London recipe against everything.

steps.title: Queenside Counter — vs ...Qb6
steps.theory: Black's ...Qb6 targets the b2 pawn your f4 bishop no longer defends. Meet it with Qb3 and c5.

steps.title: Bf5
steps.theory: Black develops the bishop to f5.

steps.title: 4.c4
steps.theory: Strike in the center with c4!

steps.title: 5.Qb3
steps.theory: Queen to b3 — offer a trade on your terms.

steps.title: 7.axb3
steps.theory: Recapture with the a-pawn. You have queenside space and an open a-file.

steps.title: Solid ...c6 Setup
steps.theory: Black plays ...c6 to support d5 without blocking the c8 bishop. Develop smoothly and keep the pressure.

steps.title: 4.Nd2
steps.theory: Nd2 avoids blocking the e-pawn and eyes e4.

steps.title: Early ...c5 vs 1...d5
steps.theory: Black skips ...Nf6 and hits c5 immediately. Stay calm — c3 and Nf3 hold everything.

steps.title: 4.c3
steps.theory: c3 locks the center — classic London.

steps.title: Safe ...Bd6 — vs ...g6
steps.theory: Smart opponents play ...g6 instead of taking on f4. Keep the queen active with Qg3.

steps.title: Bd6
steps.theory: Bd6 again — but this time Black knows the trick.

steps.title: 5.Qg3
steps.theory: Retreat the queen to g3 — keep pressure on g6 and e5.

steps.title: Symmetrical — ...Bf5 ...c6
steps.theory: When Black answers c4 with ...c6 instead of taking, hit b7 with Qb3.

steps.title: 4.Qb3
steps.theory: Queen to b3 hits b7 — the square the bishop left behind.

steps.title: KID ...Qb6 Break
steps.theory: King's Indian players love ...c5 and ...Qb6. Qb3 and c3 hold the queenside.

steps.title: 6.Qb3
steps.theory: Qb3 defends b2 and offers a trade.

steps.title: vs ...Nc6 (no ...c5)
steps.theory: Black develops the knight to c6 before ...c5. Continue normal London development.

steps.title: Early ...c5 vs ...e6
steps.theory: When Black plays ...c5 before ...Nf6 in a ...d5 ...e6 setup, Nbd2 is the modern answer.

steps.title: 5.Nd2
steps.theory: Nbd2 — the main-line way to meet ...c5.

steps.title: Prophylactic ...h6
steps.theory: Black plays ...h6 to prevent Ng5 ideas. Ignore it and finish development.

steps.title: Queenside ...a6
steps.theory: Black prepares ...b5 expansion. Keep building your pyramid.

steps.title: Queenside ...b6
steps.theory: Black fianchettos the queen's bishop. Develop normally — your structure is still better.

steps.title: vs ...Nbd7
steps.theory: Black develops the queen's knight early. Standard London continues.

steps.title: vs ...Be7
steps.theory: Black develops the bishop to e7 instead of ...Bd6. No tricks needed — just develop.

steps.title: Early ...Qd6
steps.theory: Black develops the queen early to ...d6. Keep developing — it's not a real threat.

steps.title: Qd6
steps.theory: Qd6 looks active but exposes the queen.

steps.title: Poisoned Pawn — ...Qxb2
steps.theory: If Black grabs the b2 pawn with ...Qxb2, Nb5 wins it back with interest — fork on c7 is coming.

steps.title: 5.Nb5
steps.theory: Nb5! Threatening Nc7+ forking king and rook. Black is in trouble.

steps.title: Benoni-style 1...c5
steps.theory: Black opens with ...c5 instead of ...d5. Transpose to a solid London with e3.

steps.title: Classical Order — 2.Nf3
steps.theory: The old main line still works: Nf3 before Bf4. Same structure, one tempo slower.

steps.title: 3.Bf4
steps.theory: Now Bf4 — the traditional London order.

steps.title: Bishop Pin — vs ...Bg4
steps.theory: Black pins your knight with ...Bg4. Break it with h3 — simple and effective.

steps.title: 4.h3
steps.theory: h3 asks the bishop to declare itself.

steps.title: Knight Jump — vs ...Ne4
steps.theory: Black jumps the knight to e4 early. Kick it with Nd2 and keep your structure.

steps.title: 4.Nd2
steps.theory: Nd2 kicks the knight and develops — perfect London move.
